title: First-run Schema Hints & Inline Validation Overlay for Structured Output Quickstart
creator: Amira Chen
description: Design a lightweight, first-run experience that teaches developers how to use JSON Schema with Redwood's structured-output features. Deliver a set of compact UI assets: hint 'chips' that explain common schema attributes, an inline validation overlay that surfaces schema mismatches in the Console quickstart, sample toggles (strict vs permissive), and screenshots for the release notes.
background: We currently surface structured-output in docs but lack an integrated onboarding flow in the Console quickstart that demonstrates schema validation live. Engineering will ship the validation overlay and API hooks; design provides the visuals, copy, and annotated specs. Goal: reduce initial friction and incorrect schema usage observed in 2024 support tickets.
goals: Provide a single-screen first-run module showing: example schema -> model-generated example -> inline validation annotations
Create reusable visual components (hint chips, overlay cards, toast patterns) for Console and docs
Ship accessible PNG/SVG assets and annotated Figma file for implementation
Produce release screenshots and a short in-app tour script for the Console quickstart
out_of_scope: Full schema authoring UI (this is only the first-run hints/validation overlay)
Backend schema generation from prompts (research needed separately)
design_workflow: Wireframes: quick iterations showing overlay placement (right rail vs centered modal)
High-fidelity comps: Figma frames for light/dark modes and accessible color variants
Annotated spec: spacing, token sizes, aria labels, keyboard focus order
Export assets: PNG previews for release notes, SVG icons for hint chips, and a small animated GIF demo
deliverables: Figma: DES-8462 / Console - Schema Quickstart (frames + components)
Spec doc: annotated copy + CSS tokens (Confluence link)
Microcopy: tooltip strings and error messages for i18n team
design_decisions: Use a semi-transparent left-aligned overlay anchored to the sample output instead of a blocking modal to keep user context
Validation badges: green/amber/red with explicit details on hover rather than inline verbose errors
Provide a 'Generate example' CTA that runs the model with the current schema to produce a live example; default to curated examples if user has zero credit
Two validation modes: Strict (schema enforced) and Permissive (annotated suggestions). Default to Permissive during first-run to avoid blocking experimentation
tradeoffs: Overlay vs modal: overlay keeps context but is harder to implement responsively; modal is simpler but disruptive
Live model examples increase developer understanding but add complexity for offline/private deployments — fallback to curated examples required
Showing detailed validation messages inline could overwhelm users; we prefer progressive disclosure (badge -> hover -> panel)
acceptance_criteria: Figma file with labeled components and tokens shared to engineering and PM
Two annotated screenshots (light/dark) exported at 2x for release notes
Copy finalized and approved by PM and content designer
Front-end developer checklist: aria-labels, keyboard nav, color contrast >= 4.5:1
Demo PR: small feature branch with screenshots attached and UX sign-off comment
implementation_notes: Overlay should respond to Console 'compact' and 'expanded' editor widths
Use CSS variables from the Console theme; provide fallback tokens in spec doc
Animation: subtle slide-in from the sample output with reduced motion preference respected
Provide a test hook data-testid="schema-quickstart-overlay" for e2e screenshots
